messages:
maria: Seeing a p95/p99 spike on hosted API in eu-west starting ~10:12UTC. Queue depth jumped from ~4 to ~48. Latency graphs attached to dashboard look like a queuing stall + backend CPU tail. @aj @kevin can you take a look? :eyes:
aj: On it. Dashboard shows ingress surge at 10:10, but rate-limiter counts are flat. No obvious client-side retry flood. Suspect runtime internal slowdowns.
kevin: Quick glance at runtime metrics: kernel selector churned during the window, aux_kernel usage jumped to ~40% of requests for the model group. KV cache eviction rate also rose ~3x. Could be short-seq traffic pattern flipping heuristics.
maria: any recent deploys?
deploy-bot: "deploy service/runtime v1.42.0 - success - 2025-03-12T10:05:18Z"
aj: No config pushes since then. I launched a lightweight perf sample on worker-23 (eu-west). Attaching summary: 
```
perf-sample (30s):
attn_fused_v2           42%  (hot)
matmul_qk_fp16         21%
aux_kernel_generic     18%  (higher latency)
other                  19%
```

aj: Also saw batching occupancy drop — batch sizes fell from median 8 -> 2 during spike, but queue depth rose. Means requests are waiting but not coalescing.
kevin: That combo points to kernel selector switching to aux kernels when it detects short sequences; aux kernel has lower throughput and higher tail. If traffic becomes lots of short prompts, selector mispredictions + kvcache churn cause tail.
devon: Can we force primary kernel affinity for the impacted model group and throttle prefetch sampler ramp to reduce eviction noise?
lee: I agree. Quick mitigation: pin kernel affinity for models/model-alpha to primary for seq_len<=512 and reduce prefetch threads from 4 -> 2 in eu-west canary.
aj: Pushed canary config change to 2 hosts at 10:30 UTC:
```
# canary override
model: model-alpha
kernel_affinity: primary
prefetch_threads: 2
```

aj: Monitoring: p99 dropped from ~1.8s -> ~390ms within 5 minutes on canaries. Queue depth normalizing.
maria: Nice. Can we roll to 25% while we validate? Also create follow-up for selector heuristics.
kevin: Filing INF-3241: "kernel-selector mispredict under short-seq surge -> aux kernel fallback and KV cache churn". Action items: 1) telemetry for seq-length histogram in selector (prod). 2) tighten selection thresholds, 3) long-term work: kernel cost model re-calibration and kvcache prefetch backpressure. Assigned to kevin.
sre-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 10:36 UTC, monitoring phase started. :white_check_mark:
maria: Good catch team. Postmortem & perf profile dump attached to INF-3241, will follow up with timeline and measurement graphs.
deploy-bot: Incident closure message queued for channel and statuspage.
